title: Phase 4: Integrate agents, search, and Markdown export
description: After foundation validation, integrate weaving and evolution through the same domain operations, and complete the daemon search/export capabilities before visual implementation. Use the agreed tree/addendum model, searchable agent responses, search filters/sorts, categorized discovered links, Simple tree export, and strictly read-only Agentic export. First discuss unresolved product behavior: one response associated with multiple developments and its search destination; stop/failure/retry semantics; Agentic effort levels and any model mapping. This is not authorization to choose those behaviors silently. Source of truth: .lore/context/architecture.md and the related context files. Keep business rules independent of screens. No implementation is requested by creation of this tracking issue. Before implementing the sequence, use a dedicated working branch and checkpoint each completed, verified bead. Do not push or sync without approval.
acceptance_criteria: Resolve and record the listed design questions before implementation; then split into executable child work as needed. Verify agent context excludes rejected notes/connections, thoughts stay immutable, agents cannot reject/restore, and Agentic export cannot write knowledge. Test search contracts and both Markdown export modes, and extend Bun scripts so the user can validate these features without UI.
notes:
User requirement added during Phase 1: search must use SQLite FTS5. Recorded in .lore/context/search-view.md. FTS5 is the full-text foundation; bounded typo tolerance and recorded acronym/alias matching need complementary handling rather than being assumed native FTS5 features. Search remains Phase 4 scope.
Supersedes earlier acronym/alias note: user clarified acronym matching is a future enhancement, NOT a V1 requirement. Do not build mandatory alias/expansion infrastructure or let its efficiency block V1. FTS5 remains required. Updated search-view.md and moved weaver alias recording to future possibilities. Typo tolerance has not been separately removed from the context.
Search starting point clarified by user: FTS5 plus spellfix1 for modest typo tolerance, based on previous reasonably successful search. Evaluate that baseline first rather than reinventing search. Verify spellfix1 extension availability/integration with Bun SQLite; do not assume it is built in. Exact implementation left to builder. Acronym matching remains deferred beyond V1.

title: Phase 5: Build the Next.js and React visual client
description: Build the visual client only after the daemon capabilities are established and independently testable. Use approved mockup layouts, not their colors/imagery or rejected extra navigation. Browser traffic goes through the Next.js server to the daemon. Keep this a client-only implementation scope; if a needed capability is missing, stop and discuss rather than modify the daemon/model within the visual task. Before execution, settle the visual direction and remaining client interaction details. Settings contents remain explicitly undecided; do not invent them. Source of truth: .lore/context/architecture.md and the related context files. Keep business rules independent of screens. No implementation is requested by creation of this tracking issue. Before implementing the sequence, use a dedicated working branch and checkpoint each completed, verified bead. Do not push or sync without approval.
acceptance_criteria: After design discussion, implement and verify Capture, Search/Explore, Idea, Evolve, export access, and basic Explore/Capture/Settings navigation against the established daemon contracts. Validate browser/server/daemon separation and key user flows. UI changes must not require domain rewrites; capability gaps are escalated. Keep Settings contents undecided unless separately agreed.

title: Phase 1: Establish domain logic and SQL storage
description: Build the no-AI, no-UI foundation: immutable user/AI thoughts; one evolution parent per non-root thought; branches; separate categorized connection links; user-only single and branch rejection/restoration; retained history and AI exclusion boundaries. SQL engine/schema are implementation choices to establish from the context, not assumed existing decisions. Scope is domain and persistence, not screens or agent behavior. Source of truth: .lore/context/architecture.md and the related context files. Keep business rules independent of screens. No implementation is requested by creation of this tracking issue. Before implementing the sequence, use a dedicated working branch and checkpoint each completed, verified bead. Do not push or sync without approval.
design: Phase 1 plan: greenfield Bun/TypeScript using built-in bun:sqlite; no Hono routes, UI, real agents, search or export implementation. Keep domain contracts/business rules separate from SQLite adapter. Slice A: immutable thought records, one-parent trees, separate categorized connections, schema/bootstrap and durable persistence. Slice B: user-authorized single/branch rejection and subtree restoration, branch preview/confirmation, separately rejected connections, human history vs AI-filtered read boundary. Validation: test-owned domain inputs/mocked repository dependencies for unit algorithms plus isolated SQLite integration fixtures, storage constraints and reopen persistence. Red-green per slice with separate read-only test runner; fresh oracle bun-typescript-reviewer per slice; final combined test/typecheck once. Implementation and test author: fixer; independent test execution: separate fixer invocation; review: oracle. SQL engine is SQLite based on local greenfield daemon needs and available Bun support. Preserve preexisting architecture.md change outside checkpoint commit unless explicitly included later.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled-input unit tests and isolated SQL integration tests verify immutability, single-parent ancestry, separate connection links, reject-single preserving descendants, confirmed branch scope/count, subtree restoration, independently rejected connections remaining rejected, and exclusion of rejected material from AI-facing reads. No real AI or visual client.
notes:
User authorized planning and implementation of Phase 1 only. Claimed on branch work/daemon-foundation. Phase 1 user-only rejection means a user actor may reject any authorship; AI actors cannot reject or restore. Later phases remain untouched.
Slice A RED verified independently: bun test tests/domain.test.ts tests/sqlite.test.ts -> 0 pass/12 fail from explicit unimplemented domain operations and migration bootstrap; bun run typecheck passed. Corrected broad-toThrow false positives before production handoff. Downstream SQL invariants not yet reached and require GREEN verification. Production Slice A implementation dispatched; no Phase 2 work started. User added SQLite FTS5 requirement to search context and Phase 4 bead; search remains later scope.
Slice A accepted after BTS-001 correction: 25 tests pass, 142 assertions, typecheck pass. Fresh oracle verification confirmed immutable thought sources and retained responses, seal protections, legacy/idempotent migration, REPLACE protection; no material issues. Slice B test-authoring started for user-only single/branch rejection/restoration, confirmation, mutable state and AI-safe read projections. No Hono/UI/search work.
Completed Phase 1 on work/daemon-foundation. Final independent validation: bun install --frozen-lockfile (no changes), bun test (40 pass/0 fail, 223 assertions across 4 files), bun run typecheck, git diff --check all pass. Independent bun-typescript-reviewer accepted immutable storage and rejection/AI-safe read integration; BTS-001 provenance/response immutability fixed and verified incl legacy migration, seals and REPLACE probes. README documents setup, internal raw-store boundary and absent HTTP/UI/AI/search/export surfaces. Checkpoint includes Phase1 source/tests/tooling plus daemon-first/SQLite architecture note; separate future-search/weaver context edits remain unstaged. No Phase 2 implementation.
close_reason: Implemented and independently verified immutable SQLite/domain foundation, user-only rejection/restoration, confirmed branch operations and AI-safe reads. All 40 tests and typecheck pass; code review accepted.

title: Phase 2: Expose the foundation through a Hono API
description: Expose the verified phase-1 domain operations through a Hono daemon running with Bun. Keep transport handlers separate from business logic and make the operations usable without a browser. The eventual browser must use the Next.js server, never access the daemon directly. This phase covers the foundation API, not the full later agent/search/export surface. Source of truth: .lore/context/architecture.md and the related context files. Keep business rules independent of screens. No implementation is requested by creation of this tracking issue. Before implementing the sequence, use a dedicated working branch and checkpoint each completed, verified bead. Do not push or sync without approval.
acceptance_criteria: API contract tests exercise creation, tree inspection, connection access, and user-authorized rejection/restoration against phase-1 rules, including branch preview/count and confirmation behavior. Boundary attempts and outcomes are logged. API handlers do not duplicate domain rules or introduce screen-shaped storage.

title: Phase 3: Provide practical Bun scripts for daemon testing
description: Provide simple runnable Bun scripts that exercise the phase-2 daemon API directly. The user should be able to capture thoughts, construct example evolution branches without real AI, inspect them, and reject/restore selected thoughts and subtrees. Scripts need useful output and instructions, not a polished CLI. They complement automated tests. Extend them with search and export scenarios as those capabilities arrive in phase 4; those features are not prerequisites for this foundation milestone. Source of truth: .lore/context/architecture.md and the related context files. Keep business rules independent of screens. No implementation is requested by creation of this tracking issue. Before implementing the sequence, use a dedicated working branch and checkpoint each completed, verified bead. Do not push or sync without approval.
acceptance_criteria: Document and run a reproducible foundation scenario against isolated test data, including an active descendant of a rejected thought and partial subtree restoration. Commands report results/failures clearly, require no visual client or real AI, and do not bypass daemon business rules. Existing automated tests remain in place.
